selector.rationale: The large, fluid-filled lesion with a thin wall and no septations or solid components, as seen on ultrasound and CT, is most consistent with a cystadenofibroma, which is a type of ovarian tumor.

rejected.label: Mucinous cystadenoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence in the vignette to support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Serous cystadenoma
rejected.why: Similar to mucinous cystadenoma, there is not enough specific evidence to support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Ovarian fibroma
rejected.why: The presence of a large, fluid-filled lesion is not typical of ovarian fibroma, which is usually a solid tumor

support_spans: Transvaginal ultrasound demonstrated an 18 cm diameter ovarian tumor
a large, fluid-filled lesion measuring 19.3 × 6.2 × 21 cm, located in the pelvis and mid-abdomen, displacing the uterus and compressing the aorta and inferior vena cava
The lesion appeared unilocular with a 1.5 mm wall and no septations or solid components, and was suggestive of an ovarian origin
